hostnames.title: Client Hostnames
hostnames.description: Look up a name for each client address on your network's DNS server
hostnames.toggleDescription: Ask your network's DNS servers for the name behind each client address and show that name in place of the address. This needs a reverse record for each address (sometimes labeled PTR) - pointing a name at an address is not enough on its own. Off by default. Nicknames always win over hostnames.
hostnames.guestAccessDescription: Off by default. A guest sees a view of the cache, not a list of the machines on your network, so guest sessions are shown raw addresses until you turn this on.
hostnames.routerLookupLabel: Ask the router on each client subnet
hostnames.routerLookupDescription: On by default. Asks the .1 and .254 of each subnet a client was seen in, which is where a home router publishes the names it hands out over DHCP. These are the only addresses the app works out for itself rather than reading from its own configuration. Turn it off to keep the app talking only to DNS servers someone configured.
hostnames.dockerLookupDescription: On by default. Looks for running containers that publish DNS port 53, and asks the Docker host itself. Turn it off to keep client name lookups away from the Docker socket entirely.
hostnames.settingsSaved: Saved. Client names will be looked up again.
hostnames.resolverDescription: Leave this empty and the app works out which servers to ask on its own: the DNS servers this host is configured to use, the gateways it routes through, the Docker host, containers publishing port 53, and the usual router addresses on each client's subnet. Fill it in when the server holding your reverse records is none of those. Only a private or loopback address is accepted, so names never leave your network.
hostnames.reasonNoResolver: No DNS server could be found to ask for client names. Name one above and it will be asked directly.
hostnames.reasonNoRecords: Your DNS server answered, but it has no reverse record for any of these addresses. A rewrite that points a name at an address is not enough - the server also needs a separate reverse record, sometimes called a PTR record, that points the address back to a name.
hostnames.reasonResolverTimeout: Your DNS server did not give a usable answer, so client names could not be looked up right now.
hostnames.reasonSomeUnnamed: Some clients could not be named, so they still show as numbers. Their addresses have no reverse record on your DNS server, sometimes called a PTR record.
hostnames.reasonStillLooking: Still looking up names for some clients. This will update on its own shortly.
hostnames.reasonTooManyClients: There are more clients on your network than can be looked up at one time, so the rest still show as numbers. The most recently active clients are the ones that get names.

epicMapping.description: Refreshes the Epic Games Store catalog used to identify Epic downloads in your cache: game titles and CDN URL patterns.
epicMapping.summary: Keeps the Epic Games Store catalog up to date.
epicMapping.gain: Newly released or updated Epic games are mapped to their cached downloads sooner, allowing them to appear in the game list without waiting for the next detection cycle
epicMapping.loss: New or renamed Epic games may not appear in the game list until the next scheduled refresh

xboxMapping.description: Refreshes the Xbox / Microsoft Store catalog used to name Xbox downloads in your cache. Reads the owned-games list and per-file CDN patterns from the signed-in Xbox account or an authenticated Xbox prefill session, with no prefill download required.
xboxMapping.summary: Keeps the Xbox catalog up to date.
xboxMapping.gain: Owned Xbox games are mapped to their cached downloads on a schedule, so titles downloaded on a real Xbox or PC are named without starting a prefill
xboxMapping.loss: Newly acquired Xbox games may not appear in the game list until the next scheduled refresh or a daemon login
xboxMapping.signInWaitingHelp: Waiting for you to approve the device code. Run Now stays unavailable until the sign-in finishes, is cancelled, or expires.

logRotation.description: Tells nginx to reopen its access log. Fixes the case where log rotation leaves nginx writing to a deleted file and your stats stop updating.
logRotation.summary: Reopens the nginx access log so stats keep updating.
logRotation.gain: Nginx reliably reattaches to the log file, ensuring download activity is captured correctly
logRotation.loss: If nginx has lost log access, new download activity will not be recorded until the next rotation run

cacheReconciliation.description: Compares your cache directory against the database to see what is still on disk vs. what nginx has evicted. Keeps the 'evicted' badges in the UI accurate.
cacheReconciliation.summary: Checks which cached files nginx has evicted.
cacheReconciliation.gain: Eviction badges and cache status in the UI are more accurate and up to date
cacheReconciliation.loss: The UI may show stale eviction status - items marked as cached might actually be evicted, or vice versa

cacheSizeScan.description: Walks the entire cache directory and totals every file on disk (mapped and unmapped). Updates the Cache Files dashboard stat, scan timestamp, and unmapped-cache hint.
cacheSizeScan.summary: Totals every cached file on disk.
cacheSizeScan.gain: File counts and unmapped-cache totals stay current without starting a manual scan in Management → Cache
cacheSizeScan.loss: The Cache Files stat and unmapped-cache subtitle may stay outdated until the next scan runs

gameDetection.description: Scans your cache directory and labels each chunk of cached data with the game it belongs to, using the Steam and Epic depot mappings. Incremental scans skip games already detected; previously 'Unknown' depots are resolved as new mappings arrive.
gameDetection.summary: Labels cached data with the game it belongs to.
gameDetection.gain: Newly downloaded games appear in the game list sooner, and previously unknown depots are resolved as new mappings arrive
gameDetection.loss: Games downloaded between scans won't show up in the game list until the next detection run

gameImageFetch.description: Downloads the cover art shown next to each detected game. Fills in missing artwork and refreshes any image older than 7 days, trying multiple Steam and Epic CDNs.
gameImageFetch.summary: Downloads cover art for detected games.
gameImageFetch.gain: Game cards get their artwork faster and stale images are kept up to date
gameImageFetch.loss: Some game cards may display without artwork for longer until the next image fetch cycle

cacheSnapshot.description: Saves a periodic snapshot of used cache size and total capacity so the dashboard can chart growth over time. Snapshots older than 90 days (configurable) are deleted automatically.
cacheSnapshot.summary: Records cache usage over time for the dashboard chart.
cacheSnapshot.gain: The cache growth chart has finer granularity, making it easier to spot trends and spikes
cacheSnapshot.loss: The growth chart will have wider gaps between data points, making short-term trends harder to see

operationHistoryCleanup.description: Removes cache-clear operation records older than 24 hours from the history page. Doesn't touch your actual cache files - those are only cleared from the Cache Management page.
operationHistoryCleanup.summary: Clears cache-clear records older than 24 hours.
operationHistoryCleanup.gain: Completed operation records are automatically cleaned up after 24 hours, keeping the history tidy
operationHistoryCleanup.loss: Operation records older than 24 hours are permanently removed and cannot be reviewed later

dashboardCacheWarmer.description: Pre-loads dashboard data (active downloads, stats, metrics) in the background so the page opens instantly instead of waiting on a cold database query.
dashboardCacheWarmer.summary: Preloads dashboard data so the page opens instantly.
dashboardCacheWarmer.gain: Dashboard opens immediately even after the server has been idle; users never see a cold-fetch spinner
dashboardCacheWarmer.loss: A small amount of background CPU is used each cycle, and cached values may briefly lag real-time changes until the next warm
